We don't live in a world where goods and services will be made available if there is no profit in it. That is simply human nature and will not change. But it can actually work out pretty well. The profit motive drives people to produce, but there is this thing called competition that helps to set an appropriate price. See, if you produce something that everybody needs, then you can charge whatever you want for it and people will pay. That is, until someone else, also driven by profit motive decides to provide the same thing at a lower cost. Then people will start going to that other person to get it. You, not wanting to lose all your business decide to compete by lowering your prices also. Now the two of you get into a pricing war until the price you charge reaches an equilibrium where the profit you make is still worth the effort and resources required, yet low enough to keep a consumer base. This also helps to increase efficiency because if one of you finds a way to provide the same thing with less effort or resources, you can increase your profit margin, and/or lower your prices to increase your consumer base. This means the both of you will continually search for more efficient means of production, over time driving prices down.

The big problem here is that this system is incredibly dependent on the existence of competition.
